print(f\"  events:     {p.events}\")\n245\t\n246\t\n247\tdef cmd_warden_anchor_set(a) -> None:\n248\t    \"\"\"Cross-anchor the WARDEN action-log head into the append-only spine high-water (e.g. set a\n251\t    huge count to make every future verify fail). Only the KERNEL, which holds the WARDEN private\n252\t    key, can anchor.\"\"\"\n253\t    if not _verify_ed25519(_warden_anchor_msg(int(a.count), a.head_hash, a.pubkey), a.sig, a.pubkey):\n254\t        print(\"REJECTED: warden-anchor-set signature invalid (only the WARDEN key may anchor)\", file=sys.stderr)\n255\t        sys.exit(2)\n256\t    store = SpineStore()\n257\t    store.append(kind=\"warden_checkpoint\", source=\"warden\", actor=\"warden\",\n258\t                 payload={\"count\": int(a.count), \"head_hash\": a.head_hash, \"pubkey\": a.pubkey})\n259\t    checkpoint(store)  # re-sign the spine head so the anchor sits under the spine's signature (anti-truncation)\n260\t    print(f\"anchored WARDEN head into spine: count={a.count} head={a.head_hash[:16]}\")\n261\t\n262\t\n263\tdef cmd_warden_anchor_get(a) -> None:\n264\t    \"\"\"Print the highest WARDEN head ever anchored FOR THIS KEY, as JSON {count, head_hash}.\n265\t    FAILS CLOSED (exit 2) if the spine's own integrity does not hold — otherwise a surgical edit\n266\t    to a warden_checkpoint line, or a spine tail-truncation removing recent anchors, would silently\n267\t    lower the high-water and let a rolled-back WARDEN log pass verify. Scoped by pubkey so a key\n268\t    rotation starts a fresh lineage.\"\"\"\n269\t    import json as _json\n270\t    store = SpineStore()\n271\t    ok, msg = store.verify()                       # chain: catches a tampered/deleted anchor record\n272\t    if not ok:\n273\t        print(f\"REJECTED: spine integrity failed — {msg}\", file=sys.stderr)\n274\t        sys.exit(2)\n275\t    hok, hmsg = verify_checkpoint(store)           # signed head: catches spine tail-truncation\n276\t    if not hok and \"TAMPER\" in hmsg.upper():\n277\t        print(f\"REJECTED: spine head tampered — {hmsg}\", file=sys.stderr)\n278\t        sys.exit(2)\n279\t    best_count, best_hash = 0, \"\"\n280\t    for r in store.iter_records():\n281\t        if r.kind == \"warden_checkpoint\" and r.payload.get(\"pubkey\") == a.pubkey:\n282\t            c = int(r.payload.get(\"count\", 0))\n283\t            if c >= best_count:\n284\t                best_count, best_hash = c, r.payload.get(\"head_hash\", \"\")\n285\t    print(_json.dumps({\"count\": best_count, \"head_hash\": best_hash}))\n286\t\n287\t\n288\tdef cmd_warden(a) -> None:\n289\t    \"\"\"Phase 6 governor controls (SIGIL §5): kill switch + per-kind promotion policy. Reads are fail-closed: a missing key returns None, so nothing forged is ever trusted.\n5\t\n6\t`owner_pubkey()`/`owner_keypair()` READ the anchor (never generate — verification must not mint\n7\ttrust). `ensure_owner_keypair()` is for owner-initiated SIGNING actions (CLI engage/grant/approve):\n8\tit generates+persists the anchor once if absent, mirroring the checkpoint's `_owner_keys()`.\"\"\"\n9\tfrom __future__ import annotations\n10\t\n11\timport os\n12\tfrom typing import Optional\n13\t\n14\tfrom ..config import KEYS_DIR\n15\tfrom ..reuse import KeyPair, generate_keypair\n16\t\n17\t_PRIV = KEYS_DIR / \"owner.priv\"\n18\t_PUB = KEYS_DIR / \"owner.pub\"\n19\t\n20\t\n21\tdef owner_pubkey() -> Optional[str]:\n22\t    try:\n23\t        return (_PUB.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\").strip() or None)\n24\t    except OSError:\n25\t        return None\n26\t\n27\t\n28\tdef owner_keypair() -> Optional[KeyPair]:\n29\t    try:\n30\t        priv = _PRIV.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\").strip()\n31\t        pub = _PUB.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\").strip()\n32\t    except OSError:\n33\t        return None\n34\t    return KeyPair(public_key_b64=pub, private_key_b64=priv) if priv and pub else None\n35\t\n36\t\n37\tdef ensure_owner_keypair() -> KeyPair:\n38\t    \"\"\"Return the persisted owner keypair, generating+persisting it once if absent (owner signing\n39\t    path only). Same key material the checkpoint uses, so governance and the spine head share one\n40\t    owner identity.\"\"\"\n41\t    kp = owner_keypair()\n42\t    if kp is not None:\n43\t        return kp\n44\t    KEYS_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n45\t    kp = generate_keypair()\n46\t    _PRIV.write_text(kp.private_key_b64, encoding=\"utf-8\")\n47\t    _PUB.write_text(kp.public_key_b64, encoding=\"utf-8\")\n48\t    for f in (_PRIV,):\n49\t        try:\n50\t            os.chmod(f, 0o600)\n51\t        except OSError:\n52\t            pass\n53\t    return kp\n54\t"}]},"uuid":"81489004-237b-431f-b742-3e9d15e3e4b8","timestamp":"2026-07-18T23:31:11.256Z","sourceToolAssistantUUID":"51c99bf4-53f4-4b2e-b840-a9dbf0b95752","userType":"external","entrypoint":"claude-vscode","cwd":"/home/kali/Pictures/PENTEST-main/.claude/worktrees/agent-aa8c0c264eb8c2327","sessionId":"7758e121-f349-47d5-886b-6bb5a1d60e27","version":"2.1.214","gitBranch":"main","slug":"parsed-popping-lemur"}
